info.name: ATW Backend — Company
info.description:
# ATW Backend — Company

Admin-facing company lifecycle management: company CRUD (with automatic OWNER login-account provisioning + invite email on create), the `PENDING_VERIFICATION → ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED`/`REJECTED` approval-status lifecycle (single + bulk), GST-number verification against a real vendor, the address sub-resource (a company's registered office plus any number of branches), bulk delete, and Excel (.xlsx) export.

Company **documents** and the company-user **self-service login/auth flow** (accept-invite, login, OTP, refresh, etc.) are a separate, not-yet-built module slice - every endpoint below is admin-side only. Company creation always provisions exactly one OWNER account and queues it an invite email, but accepting that invite is out of scope here.

**Run order:** Get a bearer token first (Login / Verify OTP in ATW-Auth-Account), then seed an Industry from ATW-Masterdata (`{{industryId}}`) - Create Company needs a real one. State/city ids (`{{stateId}}`/`{{cityId}}`) are pre-seeded reference data (36 states/UTs, 784 districts) - see ATW-Masterdata's Geography folder if you need to look one up. Company Profile's **Create Company** then populates `{{companyId}}`, which every other folder in this collection depends on; Company Addresses' **Add Company Address** similarly populates `{{addressId}}`. Save **Company Deletion** for last - several requests above need `{{companyId}}` to still exist, and Delete additionally needs the company's status to already be something other than `ACTIVE` (Company Status's own **Change Company Status** request, earlier in this run, already takes care of that).

**Shared conventions across every request in this collection:**
- Every endpoint requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` **and** its own specific `company.*` permission - there is no endpoint here usable by a bare authenticated caller.
- `{id}` in every path below is a company id (UUID); an unknown one always comes back `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, message "Company not found" - documented once here, not repeated on every request.
- Two response shapes exist for a company: the full `CompanyResponse` (Get Company, and every write endpoint that returns one - owner reference, every address) and the lighter `CompanySummaryResponse` (the List row - no owner, no addresses).
- GST/PAN numbers are encrypted at rest and **masked** in every response (e.g. `**********1234`) unless the caller also holds `company.view_sensitive` - same sensitivity gate the `kyc`/`worker` modules use for their own sensitive numbers. This applies to Get/List/Create/Update responses **and** to the Excel export's GST Number/PAN Number columns.
- Status changes always take an **explicit target status** (`company.manage_status`), never a blind toggle - single or bulk. Allowed transitions: `PENDING_VERIFICATION ⇄ REJECTED`, `PENDING_VERIFICATION → ACTIVE`, `ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED` - every other pair (including `REJECTED → ACTIVE` directly, and `ACTIVE → REJECTED`) is rejected. A `reason` is required for `SUSPENDED`/`REJECTED`. Moving to `SUSPENDED`/`REJECTED` disables every one of the company's login accounts and revokes every one of their refresh tokens in the same transaction; moving back to `ACTIVE` re-enables them.
- Deleting a **company** is a **soft** delete (`deletedAt`) - never a real SQL `DELETE` - and is refused while the company is `ACTIVE` (change status first, e.g. to `SUSPENDED`). Every satellite row (addresses, status history, the company's own users and their tokens) is left untouched, preserving full history.
- `POST .../bulk-status` and `POST .../bulk-delete` both take a batch of ids and process each independently, by calling the exact same guarded single-item logic per id - partial success is normal; check `data.failures[]` for which id was skipped and why - same convention as ATW-Masterdata/ATW-Worker's own bulk endpoints.
- **Export returns a raw `.xlsx` file download** (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="companies.xlsx"`), **NOT** the usual JSON envelope - this is the only endpoint in this collection that isn't JSON. Give `ids` for an exact set, or any combination of List Companies' own filters to export a filtered set; post `{}` to export every company.
- A company's addresses are a genuinely variable-length list (one registered office plus any number of branches, unlike a worker's fixed 2 rows) - full sub-resource CRUD, one address at a time. Exactly one address is primary at all times once a company has any; deleting the primary auto-promotes the next-oldest survivor, and a company can never be left with zero addresses (its last one can't be deleted) or with its current primary unset with no replacement promoted in the same call.
- GST verification calls a real vendor (Sandbox.co.in's GST Compliance API) in production - see `HANDOVER.md` for the Azure configuration required to turn this on (it defaults to a deterministic stub everywhere until then).

Every JSON endpoint is versioned under `/api/v1/` and returns the same envelope:

```
{ "success": boolean, "data": <payload> | null, "error": <ApiError> | null }
```

`ApiError` shape: `{"code": string, "message": string, "fieldErrors": [{"field","message"}] | null, "timestamp": ISO-8601 string, "traceId": string | null}`. `traceId` echoes the `X-Correlation-Id` request header when present.

## Running this collection

Select the **ATW Backend - Local** environment first.

1. Run **Login** / **Verify OTP** from **ATW-Auth-Account.postman_collection.json** to populate `{{accessToken}}` - every request below requires it, plus its own `company.*` permission.
2. From **ATW-Masterdata.postman_collection.json**, run **Create Industry** (→ `{{industryId}}`) - Create Company needs a real one. `{{stateId}}`/`{{cityId}}` are pre-seeded reference data; look one up via Masterdata's Geography folder if not already set in your environment.
3. **Company Profile → Create Company** populates `{{companyId}}` - every folder below needs it.
4. **Company Addresses → Add Company Address** populates `{{addressId}}`.
5. **Company Status**, **Company GST Verification**, and the rest of **Company Addresses** can then run in any order against the same `{{companyId}}`.
6. Run **Company Deletion** (**Delete Company** / **Bulk Delete Companies**) **last** - several folders above need `{{companyId}}` to still exist, and Delete additionally needs the company's status to already be something other than `ACTIVE` (Company Status's own **Change Company Status** request, earlier in this run, already takes care of that).

## Error codes that can appear on (almost) any endpoint

These are produced centrally - by `GlobalExceptionHandler`, by Spring Security's entry point/access-denied handler, or by security filters that run before a controller is even reached - so they are **not** re-documented on every individual request below; only an endpoint's *specific* codes/triggers are.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | A `@Valid` request-body field failed Bean Validation (`fieldErrors[]` present), or a service-level input check failed (no `fieldErrors`). |
| `MALFORMED_REQUEST` | 400 | Request body is missing or isn't valid JSON. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | No bearer token presented at all, or it's malformed/expired/signature-invalid. |
| `SESSION_REVOKED` | 401 | The token parses fine, but the admin's security version has moved on since it was issued (password changed, account disabled) - discard tokens and log in again. |
| `ACCESS_DENIED` | 403 | Authenticated, but lacking the specific `company.*` permission the endpoint requires. |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The id in the URL doesn't exist. |
| `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 | Input is syntactically well-formed but violates a business rule (e.g. deleting an ACTIVE company, an illegal status transition, unsetting the only primary address, deleting a company's last address). |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | A duplicate check failed (GST/PAN/owner email already in use) - either a friendly pre-check, or a generic last-resort fallback when a unique-constraint violation reaches the database despite an earlier check passing (a genuine race between two concurrent requests). |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected failure. Full detail is logged server-side against the same `traceId` returned to the client. |

## Documentation cross-references

- **ATW-Auth-Account.postman_collection.json** - login/2FA; needed for `{{accessToken}}` before anything here will work.
- **ATW-RBAC-Staff.postman_collection.json** - grant a role the `company.*` permissions this collection exercises. None are auto-granted to any role by default, including the brand-new `company.manage_status`/`company.delete`/`company.export` this round adds real endpoints for (the permission codes themselves were already seeded when the module first shipped).
- **ATW-Masterdata.postman_collection.json** - industries/geography; Create Company and the address endpoints reference ids created/seeded there (`{{industryId}}`, `{{stateId}}`, `{{cityId}}`).
- `HANDOVER.md` - Azure deployment context, including the GST-verification vendor's required configuration (and the same requirement for the two sibling Sandbox.co.in integrations, Aadhaar e-KYC and bank verification).

item.name: Company Profile
item.description: Core company CRUD under `/api/v1/admin/companies` - list/search, single-company detail, create (provisions the OWNER account + invite email in the same transaction), profile update, and Excel export. Permission is per request: `company.view` (List, Get), `company.create` (Create), `company.edit` (Update), `company.export` (Export). Status, addresses, and GST verification are **not** part of this folder - see the dedicated folders below for each. **Delete Company / Bulk Delete Companies live in the separate Company Deletion folder at the end of this collection** - run everything else first.

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.view`.

Paginated, multiselect-filterable (`status`, `industryId`, `stateId`, `cityId`), free-text-searchable (`search` matches `name` or `companyCode`) list, returned as the lighter `CompanySummaryResponse` (no owner, no addresses - see Get Company for those). Default sort is `createdAt,desc`.

**Filters** (all optional, all independent, repeat a query param for multiselect e.g. `?status=ACTIVE&status=PENDING_VERIFICATION`):
- `status`, `industryId`, `stateId`, `cityId` - a non-empty filter matches ANY of its own values (OR within the filter); every non-empty filter is ANDed together with the others.
- `stateId`/`cityId` (Masterdata ids, multiselect) - matches a company with ANY address referencing one of the given ids (no address-type split the way Worker has - a company's addresses carry no permanent/current distinction).
- `search` - case-insensitive substring match against name or company code.
- `gstVerified` (boolean) - `true` for GST-verified companies only, `false` for unverified only, omit for both.
- `createdFrom`/`createdTo` (plain `YYYY-MM-DD` dates, either or both) - filters on the company's creation date, interpreted as whole UTC calendar days.

**Pagination/sort:** standard Spring pagination (`page`, `size`, `sort`). `sort` only accepts real, directly-queryable columns: `name`, `companyCode`, `status`, `createdAt` - notably **not** `gstVerified`/`createdFrom`/`createdTo`/`stateId`/`cityId`, since none of those are columns on this table.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unsupported `sort` property | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 200 - OK
400 - Unsupported sort property

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.create`.

Creates the company (status `PENDING_VERIFICATION`, GST unverified) and its OWNER login account in one transaction, then enqueues an invite email to the owner (the async outbox path - a transient email-provider hiccup never rolls back the creation). GST/PAN are optional and never verified here - use Verify Company GST afterward (Company GST Verification folder).

**Validation, checked in this order:**
1. `industryId` must reference an existing industry.
2. `ownerEmail` must not already belong to another company-user account.
3. When given, `gstNumber`/`panNumber` must not already belong to another company.
4. When `addresses` is non-empty, exactly one entry must have `primary=true`.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown `industryId`, or `addresses` given with zero or more than one `primary=true` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| `ownerEmail` already in use by another company-user account | `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| `gstNumber`/`panNumber` already belongs to another company | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

This request's Tests script saves the new id to `{{companyId}}` - every other folder in this collection needs it.

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.export`.

**Returns a raw `.xlsx` file download (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="companies.xlsx"`), NOT the usual JSON envelope** - this is the only endpoint on this controller that doesn't return `ApiResponse`. Columns, in order: Company Code, Name, Industry, Status, GST Number, PAN Number, GST Verified (`Yes`/`No`), Created At. GST/PAN are masked unless the caller also holds `company.view_sensitive` - the exact same masking Get Company applies.

Give `ids` for an exact set (unknown ids are silently skipped); otherwise every other field is an optional filter with the **exact same semantics as List Companies above** (a non-empty set matches ANY of its values; every non-empty field is ANDed together). Posting `{}` exports every company, unfiltered.

**Note on the Tests script below:** it checks the response headers (content-type, filename) instead of the usual envelope checks, since this endpoint genuinely isn't JSON and Postman's sandbox can't parse .xlsx bytes directly.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Caller lacks `company.export` | `ACCESS_DENIED` | 403 |

item.name: Company Status
item.description: The company approval-status lifecycle: `PENDING_VERIFICATION ⇄ REJECTED`, `PENDING_VERIFICATION → ACTIVE`, `ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED` - every other pair (including `REJECTED → ACTIVE` directly, and `ACTIVE → REJECTED`) is rejected. Every change takes an explicit target status via `company.manage_status` (single or bulk), never a blind toggle; a `reason` is required for `SUSPENDED`/`REJECTED`. Moving to `SUSPENDED`/`REJECTED` disables every one of the company's login accounts and revokes every one of their refresh tokens in the same transaction; moving back to `ACTIVE` re-enables them. Status History is the append-only, never-edited audit trail of every transition a company has ever had.

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.manage_status`.

An explicit target status, never a blind toggle. `reason` is required when the target is `SUSPENDED` or `REJECTED`; ignored otherwise.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown company id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Target equals the current status, or `reason` missing for `SUSPENDED`/`REJECTED` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| Illegal transition (e.g. `REJECTED` -> `ACTIVE` directly, `ACTIVE` -> `REJECTED`) | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.manage_status`.

Applies the exact same guarded transition as Change Company Status (above) to every id in `ids` independently - calls the single-company logic per id, so every rule (allowed-transition check, reason-required check, the login-account disable/revoke cascade) is identical, just batched. Partial success is the normal, expected outcome, not an all-or-nothing failure - one id failing its guard (not found, illegal transition, missing reason, ...) is recorded in `data.failures[]` and does not roll back the ids that already succeeded.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` was empty | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 200 - Partial success (one illegal transition)
400 - ids was empty

item.name: Company GST Verification
item.description: Triggers a GST-number verification against the configured vendor (Sandbox.co.in's GST Compliance API in production; a deterministic stub everywhere else by default - see `HANDOVER.md`). Deliberately decoupled from company creation: creating a company never depends on this call succeeding, so a vendor outage can never block onboarding. Reuses `company.edit` rather than its own permission code, mirroring how worker bank-account verification reuses an existing code.

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.edit`.

No request body - verifies whatever `gstNumber` is currently on file for this company against the configured GST-verification provider. On success, stamps `gstVerifiedAt`/`gstVerificationRef`. A provider-reported negative result (invalid pattern, not found, not active) surfaces as a 422 with the provider's own reason and persists nothing, so this can simply be retried once the GST number on file is corrected.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown company id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| No GST number on file for this company | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| Provider reports invalid/not-found/inactive GSTIN | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |
| Provider unreachable or times out | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

response.name: 200 - Verified (stub provider)

item.name: Company Addresses
item.description: A company's addresses as a standalone sub-resource - one registered office plus any number of branches, a genuinely variable-length list (unlike a worker's fixed 2 address rows), so full CRUD (list/add/update/delete one at a time) rather than a single fixed-shape endpoint. Permission is `company.view` for List, `company.edit` for Add/Update/Delete. Exactly one address is primary at all times once a company has any: Add/Update demote whichever address currently holds primary when you set `primary=true` on a different one; Update additionally refuses to unset the CURRENT primary address unless a different one is being promoted in the same call; Delete either blocks removing a company's only remaining address outright, or auto-promotes the next-oldest survivor when the deleted address was primary.

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.edit`.

Setting `primary=true` demotes whichever address currently holds it - at most one address per company may be primary. A company may transiently have zero primary addresses right after creation if none was added yet; once at least one exists, Update/Delete both enforce exactly one primary at all times.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown company id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Unknown `stateId`/`cityId` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.edit`.

Full replace of the address at `addressId`, except its `addressType` (fixed once created). Rejected with a 422 if this address is currently the company's primary one and `primary=false` is sent with no different address being promoted in the same request - to actually change which address is primary, set `primary=true` on the new one instead; to remove the primary address entirely, delete it (which auto-promotes a replacement).

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown company id, or address doesn't belong to this company | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Unknown `stateId`/`cityId` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| Attempting to unset the current primary address with no replacement promoted | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.edit`. Soft-deletes the address (never a real SQL DELETE).

**Rules:** rejected with a 422 if this is the company's only remaining address - a company must always have at least one. If the deleted address was the primary one and another remains, the next-oldest surviving address is automatically promoted to primary in the same request.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown company id, or address doesn't belong to this company | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| This is the company's only remaining address | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

response.name: 200 - OK
422 - Only remaining address

item.name: Company Deletion
item.description: Deleting a company is a **soft** delete (`deletedAt`) - never a real SQL `DELETE` - and is refused while the company is `ACTIVE`. Every satellite row (addresses, status history, the company's own users and their tokens) is left untouched, preserving full history, and the user-disable-and-revoke-sessions cascade applies exactly as it does for a SUSPENDED/REJECTED status change. **Run this folder last** - several requests in the folders above need `{{companyId}}` to still exist.

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.delete`.

Soft-deletes the company and applies the same user-disable-and-revoke-sessions cascade as moving to SUSPENDED/REJECTED.

**Precondition:** rejected with a 422 if the company is currently `ACTIVE` - change its status first (e.g. to `SUSPENDED`) via Change Company Status, then delete.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown company id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Company is currently `ACTIVE` | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

response.name: 200 - OK
422 - Company is currently ACTIVE

request.description:
**Permission:** `company.delete`.

Applies the exact same guarded soft-delete as Delete Company (above) to every id in `ids` independently - calls the single-company logic per id. Partial success is expected - an id that's currently `ACTIVE`, or doesn't exist, is recorded in `data.failures[]` without rolling back the ids that already succeeded.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` was empty | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

response.name: 200 - Partial success (one still ACTIVE)
400 - ids was empty
